findings.issue_text: Migration query for 'embed_category' site setting crashes with NoMethodError on any site where the setting was never changed from its default, because site_settings only has a row when changed, making result[0] nil — blocking all deploys

Migration fallback query for 'uncategorized_category_id' crashes with NoMethodError when that row isn't materialized, and when it is materialized with the default empty string, .to_i yields 0, producing embeddable_hosts rows with category_id = 0 that point at no category

Migrated host values are inserted verbatim via raw SQL, so values with schemes and paths (e.g. 'http://discourse.org') skip the before_validation strip and never match record_for_host's host comparison, causing all existing embeds to fail with Discourse::InvalidAccess after deploy
SQL string interpolation of legacy host values breaks the migration outright if any value contains a quote
EmbeddableHostsController#update raises NoMethodError (unhandled 500 instead of 404) when the record id doesn't exist because save_host calls host.host= on nil
EmbeddableHostsController#destroy reports success for a nonexistent record because nil.destroy is a no-op that renders success
Fabricator contents are swapped between files: category_fabricator.rb defines the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category fabricators
EmbeddingController#update accepts and discards all input, reading nothing from params and writing nothing, so any PUT to the endpoint silently no-ops

Store.js `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code since map never returns falsy, while the real failure mode (missing side-load records producing null entries in the array, causing rendering errors in embedding.hbs) is unguarded
Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category setting is empty (default ''), because the SQL JOIN returns no rows and nil['id'] is called before the category_id == 0 fallback can trigger

Migration inserts embeddable_hosts values verbatim including http:// schemes and paths, but the new exact host comparison in EmbeddableHost.record_for_host will reject referers for existing hosts entered with schemes/paths, silently breaking the feature after upgrade
Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy crash with 500 when the given ID doesn't exist because save_host(nil) and host.destroy are called on nil without a 404 check
Migration interpolates raw setting values into INSERT SQL without sanitization, allowing SQL injection or migration failure on values containing single quotes

The contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb were accidentally swapped, putting each fabricator in the wrong file
Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing despite the route and frontend saveChanges action existing, so saving silently does nothing and returns unchanged data
No uniqueness constraint on the embeddable_hosts host column, allowing duplicate rows for the same host with different categories and nondeterministic category assignment in record_for_host

Fabricator file contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains the :embeddable_host fabricator while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the old category fabricator definitions, likely an accidental file-swap/git mv mistake masked by global Fabricator registration

The update action in admin/embedding_controller.rb is a no-op dead implementation: fetch_embedding rebuilds the record from EmbeddableHost.all and nothing is ever written, yet routes, controller, serializer usage, and frontend JS save actions all exist to serve it

Migration's embed_category data conversion joins site_settings.value to categories.name, but the setting was consumed as a category id passed to PostCreator, so the join may silently fail leaving category_id == 0 and migrating all hosts to uncategorized

Migration irreversibly and unconditionally deletes legacy site settings ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category') with no down path, even when the preceding conversion was skipped or produced a fallback category, making the original values unrecoverable

The removed SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard in topic.rb expandable_first_post? was replaced by nothing instead of an EmbeddableHost.exists? check, dropping the invariant that first-post truncation only applies while embedding is configured, and the related spec passes vacuously hiding the regression
Unrelated drive-by lint edits (unused variable removals) in topic_spec.rb digest specs have no connection to the embedding feature, polluting the diff and review surface
Locale key admin.embedding.edit is defined but never referenced by any template or component; the template uses icon-only buttons with no label, making it a dead locale entry
Admin embedding update action is a silent no-op: it re-renders the serializer without reading or persisting params, returning HTTP 200 while discarding the caller's payload

Host case normalization asymmetry: validation accepts uppercase hosts (regex with /i, no downcasing in before_validation) but record_for_host matches lower(host) = uri.host where URI host is always lowercase, so stored hosts like 'Eviltrout.com' can never match embed requests
No UNIQUE index on host (or lower(host)) in the embeddable_hosts migration, allowing the same host to be registered twice with .first arbitrarily picking one
Port is accepted by host validation regex but record_for_host compares against URI#host which excludes the port, making stored hosts with ports permanently unmatchable
Embeddable hosts controller update/destroy lack not-found guards, causing NoMethodError on nil (500) instead of 404 for stale or hand-crafted ids
category_id is assigned from params with no existence validation, no FK, and no presence check on the belongs_to :category association, allowing dead category references
Category deletion leaves embeddable_hosts rows dangling with no dependent/nullify hook, breaking TopicEmbed.import and causing embeds to fail or land in Uncategorized
category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb have their contents swapped: the category file defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) and the host file contains all the category fabricators
Migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil when 'embed_category' site setting was never set or doesn't match a category name, aborting db:migrate for default installs and blocking deploys

Migrated embeddable hosts are inserted raw via SQL, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization that strips http(s):// prefixes and paths, causing previously allowed hosts to fail matching and get Discourse::InvalidAccess on /embed/comments
Migration permanently DELETEs the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings with no rollback path, causing unrecoverable data loss if any INSERT fails midway or rollback is needed

Fabricator file contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains only the EmbeddableHost fabricator while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the Category fabricators, misleading future contributors editing the wrong file
embedding_controller.rb update action renders a serialization of the never-mutated @embedding, silently discarding all submitted changes from the PUT while responding 200 with success JSON
embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update and destroy fetch EmbeddableHost by id with no nil check, causing NoMethodError and HTTP 500 instead of a 404 or validation error for stale or fabricated ids
topic.rb expandable_first_post? dropped the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard, changing semantics so deleting all embeddable hosts no longer disables truncation for existing embedded topics
SQL string interpolation of unvalidated site setting values into raw INSERT in migration, allowing SQL injection or migration crash on single quotes
Unguarded nil on user-supplied params[:id] lookup in update and destroy actions of EmbeddableHostsController, causing unhandled 500 errors for stale or invalid ids

The entire spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController is only an ancestry assertion (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController), verifying none of the new behavior: the blank-category_id fallback to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id, the render_json_error path for invalid hosts, destroy of a nonexistent id (which would 500 on nil), or the serialization shape

Admin::EmbeddingController#update contains no persistence logic at all — it just re-renders the serialized @embedding — while the frontend saveChanges action calls update({}) expecting to save; no test issues a PUT and checks that anything changes, so the save embedding feature is a no-op that the passing suite gives false confidence about

The 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test in topic_spec.rb now verifies a branch that no longer exists after removal of the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard from Topic#expandable_first_post?; it passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false, and the new semantic (topic with has_topic_embed? and embed_truncate true is expandable even with zero hosts configured) has no coverage

The 'raises an error with a missing host' test in embed_controller_spec.rb is stale: it claims to cover host-config denial but passes only because no referer is stubbed, so the referer check fires instead; the new empty-hosts behavior (no rows in embeddable_hosts) is never directly asserted

The new plural _ids hydration branch in store.js.es6 is only tested on the happy path where all ids exist in the side-loaded payload; there is no test for an id absent from the root payload, where _lookupSubType returns null and the hydrated array silently contains null entries while the original _ids key is unconditionally deleted, crashing consumers like {{#each fruit.colors}} with unrecoverable data

The 'find embedded' test in store-test.js.es6 claims to load fruit 2 (banana, color_ids: [3]) but the pretender handler ignores the request id and always returns fruits[0] (apple, color_ids: [1,2]), so the assertions verify apple's data; the test passes only by mock accident and cannot catch hydration bugs specific to single-element color_ids arrays

The topic_embed.rb change replacing SiteSetting.embed_category with eh.try(:category_id) has only one spec assertion covering the matching-host case; no test exercises the branch where the imported URL's host is not registered (record_for_host returns nil), causing the topic to be created uncategorized instead of in the previously configured embed_category

Migration crashes with NoMethodError when the 'embed_category' setting row doesn't exist in site_settings or its value doesn't match a category name, because execute(...)[0] is nil on the default configuration
The 'uncategorized_category_id' fallback queries site_settings for a value that is a computed Ruby method on SiteSetting, not a database row, so the fallback path also crashes with NoMethodError

The migration irreversibly DELETEs the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site_settings rows inside def change with no down method, backup, or restore path, permanently losing configuration on rollback

Migrated host values are inserted verbatim without normalizing schemes/paths, so hosts stored as 'http://discourse.org' never match the new EmbeddableHost.record_for_host query comparing against uri.host, silently breaking previously-allowed embeds
Host values are interpolated into raw SQL INSERT statements without quoting or parameterization, allowing syntax errors or SQL injection from single quotes/backslashes in stored values

The deploy removes the settings from site_settings.yml and deletes SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? in the same step as the data migration, so old application servers during a rolling restart raise undefined-method/missing-setting errors with no expand/contract transitional phase

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration query for 'embed_category' site setting crashes with NoMethodError on any site where the setting was never changed from its default, because site_settings only has a row when changed, making result[0] nil — blocking all deploys

Migration fallback query for 'uncategorized_category_id' crashes with NoMethodError when that row isn't materialized, and when it is materialized with the default empty string, .to_i yields 0, producing embeddable_hosts rows with category_id = 0 that point at no category

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, the fallback does `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i`. If that `SELECT` returns zero rows (which is plausible since `site_settings` typically only stores overridden settings), indexing `[0]` yields `nil` and `nil['value']` raises `NoMethodError`. Additionally, if the row exists but `value` is an empty string, `''.to_i` becomes `0`, and the subsequent inserts use `category_id = 0`, which does not correspond to a real category. So the finding describes a real defect in the diff (missing-result handling / potential invalid category_id).

EmbeddableHostsController#update raises NoMethodError (unhandled 500 instead of 404) when the record id doesn't exist because save_host calls host.host= on nil
EmbeddableHostsController#destroy reports success for a nonexistent record because nil.destroy is a no-op that renders success

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `host.destroy`. If no record exists, `host` will be `nil`, and calling `destroy` on `nil` raises a `NoMethodError` in Ruby—it is not a no-op and will not proceed to `render json: success_json` unless an exception is rescued elsewhere (not shown in the diff). So the proposed finding mischaracterizes the behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator contents are swapped between files: category_fabricator.rb defines the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category fabricators
EmbeddingController#update accepts and discards all input, reading nothing from params and writing nothing, so any PUT to the endpoint silently no-ops

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` only calls `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads `params` or persists any changes. `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` from current DB state (`EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`), so a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` will return JSON but perform no update. This makes the PUT endpoint effectively a no-op (it “accepts” input but discards it).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store.js `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code since map never returns falsy, while the real failure mode (missing side-load records producing null entries in the array, causing rendering errors in embedding.hbs) is unguarded

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js` the `hydrated || []` fallback in the `_ids` branch is indeed effectively redundant because `Array#map` always returns an array when called. However, the claimed “real failure mode” (missing sideload records yielding `null`/`undefined` entries that then break `embedding.hbs`) is not verifiable from this diff: the new `EmbeddingSerializer` uses `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`, which in Discourse’s serializer pattern typically includes the sideloaded `embeddable_hosts` records alongside the id list, so `_lookupSubType` should resolve them. The diff does not show a case where ids are sent without corresponding sideloaded records, so the rendering-error assertion is speculative rather than a demonstrated defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category setting is empty (default ''), because the SQL JOIN returns no rows and nil['id'] is called before the category_id == 0 fallback can trigger
matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same root cause: the migration assumes the SQL query returns a row and immediately accesses ['id'], so when embed_category yields no matching rows (empty/missing setting), it ends up calling nil['id'] and crashes. This matches the golden issue about missing row checks leading to a crash and broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration inserts embeddable_hosts values verbatim including http:// schemes and paths, but the new exact host comparison in EmbeddableHost.record_for_host will reject referers for existing hosts entered with schemes/paths, silently breaking the feature after upgrade

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, existing `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` entries are inserted via raw SQL: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, so any values like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` are stored verbatim and bypass `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization (which strips scheme/path). Later, host checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(referer)` which parses the referer URL to `uri.host` (e.g., `discourse.org`, `example.com`) and then does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That exact comparison will not match rows containing schemes/paths, so previously-allowed hosts (entered with scheme/path in the old setting, which `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` explicitly supported) will be rejected after migration, breaking embedding access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy crash with 500 when the given ID doesn't exist because save_host(nil) and host.destroy are called on nil without a 404 check
Migration interpolates raw setting values into INSERT SQL without sanitization, allowing SQL injection or migration failure on values containing single quotes

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration reads embeddable_hosts from site_settings, splits by newlines into `records`, then does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. The value `h` is interpolated directly into SQL inside single quotes with no escaping/quoting helper. If an existing setting line contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters), the SQL becomes invalid and the migration can fail; additionally, because the value is inserted into raw SQL, it is susceptible to SQL injection via crafted setting content. This is a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The only tests for the new admin endpoints assert class inheritance, with no coverage of CRUD paths, category fallback, validation errors, or the EmbeddingSerializer/store hydration contract

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the only new controller specs for the admin endpoints are `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`, and both only assert the controller subclasses `Admin::AdminController`. There are no tests exercising the actual CRUD actions in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (create/update/destroy), nor the `Admin::EmbeddingController` show/update responses, nor behavior like category_id fallback or error rendering. While there are model specs for `EmbeddableHost` and some embed-related controller/spec changes, they do not cover the new admin endpoints or the serializer/store hydration contract mentioned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb were accidentally swapped, putting each fabricator in the wrong file

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb no longer defines any :category-related fabricators and instead defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while the newly added spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category, and :private_category fabricators. This is a verifiable mismatch between file names and their contents (effectively swapped), which can be a real defect if anything expects fabricators to be in the conventional file (e.g., requiring category_fabricator.rb to get :category).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing despite the route and frontend saveChanges action existing, so saving silently does nothing and returns unchanged data

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and does not read any params or persist any changes. The admin route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` is added, and the frontend controller defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would issue an update request but there is nothing server-side that actually updates anything. While the current `embedding.hbs` template doesn’t wire up `saveChanges`, the presence of the route and action means an attempted “save” would be a no-op that still returns success data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No uniqueness constraint on the embeddable_hosts host column, allowing duplicate rows for the same host with different categories and nondeterministic category assignment in record_for_host

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an `embeddable_hosts` table and `EmbeddableHost` model but does not add any uniqueness validation or DB unique index on `host` (migration defines `t.string :host, null: false` only). The lookup method `record_for_host` uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, which will return an arbitrary matching row if duplicates exist (no `order`), making the chosen record (and thus `TopicEmbed.import`'s `category: eh.try(:category_id)`) potentially nondeterministic when duplicate hosts with different categories are present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator file contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains the :embeddable_host fabricator while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the old category fabricator definitions, likely an accidental file-swap/git mv mistake masked by global Fabricator registration

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was changed to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` and the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the category-related fabricators (i.e., the contents are effectively swapped relative to filenames). However, this is not a clearly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone: Fabrication typically loads all fabricator files via a directory glob (so the fabricators would still be registered regardless of filename). The finding’s claim that this is a “mistake masked by global registration” is plausible but speculative, and no breakage is demonstrated in the diff (no code shown requiring fabricators by filename).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The update action in admin/embedding_controller.rb is a no-op dead implementation: fetch_embedding rebuilds the record from EmbeddableHost.all and nothing is ever written, yet routes, controller, serializer usage, and frontend JS save actions all exist to serve it

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` simply re-renders `@embedding` without persisting anything, and `@embedding` itself is reconstructed every request in `fetch_embedding` from `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` (an `OpenStruct`, not an AR model). Despite that, a PUT route is added (`put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`), an Ember adapter points to `/admin/customize/embedding`, and the admin controller action `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, implying there is something to save via this endpoint. As written, PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` is effectively a no-op/misleading implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration's embed_category data conversion joins site_settings.value to categories.name, but the setting was consumed as a category id passed to PostCreator, so the join may silently fail leaving category_id == 0 and migrating all hosts to uncategorized

Migration irreversibly and unconditionally deletes legacy site settings ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category') with no down path, even when the preceding conversion was skipped or produced a fallback category, making the original values unrecoverable

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration ends with `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"` unconditionally. This runs even if no `embeddable_hosts` rows were inserted (e.g., the setting was missing/blank) and even if `embed_category` lookup fails and falls back to `uncategorized_category_id`. The migration is defined with `change` and uses raw `execute`/data deletion, so Rails cannot automatically reverse it and there is no explicit `down` restoring the deleted settings. That makes legacy values unrecoverable after migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The removed SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard in topic.rb expandable_first_post? was replaced by nothing instead of an EmbeddableHost.exists? check, dropping the invariant that first-post truncation only applies while embedding is configured, and the related spec passes vacuously hiding the regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` condition from `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, but the method still gates on `has_topic_embed?`, which limits the behavior to topics that actually have an embed record. Since `embeddable_hosts` was removed from `SiteSetting` and replaced by the `EmbeddableHost` table, there’s no clear, verifiable requirement in the diff that truncation must be disabled when zero hosts are configured (it could be intentional that existing embedded topics remain truncatable based solely on `embed_truncate`). The claim that a spec now “passes vacuously hiding the regression” is also not directly supported by the shown diff. Overall this is a behavior change, but not a clearly demonstrable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated drive-by lint edits (unused variable removals) in topic_spec.rb digest specs have no connection to the embedding feature, polluting the diff and review surface

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include minor spec-only cleanups in `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` (e.g., removing unused local variable assignments like `topic = Fabricate(...)` -> `Fabricate(...)`) that are unrelated to the embedding feature. However, this is a review-surface/style/process concern rather than a bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Locale key admin.embedding.edit is defined but never referenced by any template or component; the template uses icon-only buttons with no label, making it a dead locale entry

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `admin.embedding.edit` to `client.en.yml`, but none of the added/modified templates reference that key (the `embeddable-host` component uses icon-only `d-button`s with no `label`, and the other i18n uses are `admin.embedding.host/category/add_host/confirm_delete/title`). However, calling this a “REAL problem” is overstated: an unused locale entry is at most minor cleanup/maintainability, and from the diff alone it’s not strictly provable it’s never referenced elsewhere in the codebase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embedding update action is a silent no-op: it re-renders the serializer without reading or persisting params, returning HTTP 200 while discarding the caller's payload

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action does not read `params` or persist any changes; it simply `render_serialized(@embedding, EmbeddingSerializer, ...)`, same as `show`. The PUT route (`put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`) will therefore return 200/serialized data even if the caller sends an update payload, which is effectively discarded. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host case normalization asymmetry: validation accepts uppercase hosts (regex with /i, no downcasing in before_validation) but record_for_host matches lower(host) = uri.host where URI host is always lowercase, so stored hosts like 'Eviltrout.com' can never match embed requests
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying bug: record_for_host is intended to match hosts case-insensitively but only normalizes one side of the comparison, leading to failures when either the stored host or the lookup host has mixed/upper case. The candidate explains the asymmetry (stored mixed-case vs lowercased URI host) which is the same case-normalization issue described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No UNIQUE index on host (or lower(host)) in the embeddable_hosts migration, allowing the same host to be registered twice with .first arbitrarily picking one

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with `host` and `category_id` but does not add any uniqueness constraint/index on `host` (or `lower(host)`). The model also lacks a `validates_uniqueness_of :host`. Lookups use `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, so if duplicate rows exist for the same host (case-insensitively), `.first` will return an arbitrary row, which can lead to inconsistent behavior (e.g., category selection for embedded topics). This is a concrete correctness issue enabled by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Port is accepted by host validation regex but record_for_host compares against URI#host which excludes the port, making stored hosts with ports permanently unmatchable

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the `validates_format_of :host` regex explicitly allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`). The `before_validation` callback strips scheme and path but does not strip the port, so a value like `example.com:3000` can be saved. However, `record_for_host(host)` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host`, which excludes the port (it would be `example.com`). The lookup `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` will therefore never match a stored `example.com:3000`, making port-bearing stored hosts unmatchable and causing `host_allowed?` to incorrectly reject them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embeddable hosts controller update/destroy lack not-found guards, causing NoMethodError on nil (500) instead of 404 for stale or hand-crafted ids

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController, both update and destroy fetch with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately use the result without checking for nil. In `update`, `save_host(host)` will call `host.host = ...` and `host.category_id = ...`, which will raise `NoMethodError` if no record exists. In `destroy`, `host.destroy` will similarly raise if host is nil. This would yield a 500 for stale/invalid IDs rather than a proper 404/RecordNotFound handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: category_id is assigned from params with no existence validation, no FK, and no presence check on the belongs_to :category association, allowing dead category references

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host, `host.category_id` is set directly from `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` (or uncategorized if blank) with no check that the referenced Category exists. The `EmbeddableHost` model only declares `belongs_to :category` and a host format validation; it does not validate presence/existence of `category`/`category_id`. The migration makes `category_id` `null: false` but does not add a foreign key constraint, so a non-null but non-existent `category_id` can be persisted, creating dead references.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Category deletion leaves embeddable_hosts rows dangling with no dependent/nullify hook, breaking TopicEmbed.import and causing embeds to fail or land in Uncategorized
category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb have their contents swapped: the category file defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) and the host file contains all the category fabricators
matched_golden_ids: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly states that category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb have their contents swapped (category defines :embeddable_host and host contains category fabricators), which is the same underlying issue as the golden comment about swapped files causing loss/misplacement of the original fabricators and potential errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil when 'embed_category' site setting was never set or doesn't match a category name, aborting db:migrate for default installs and blocking deploys

adjudication.rationale: Real issue in `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`: it does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If the query returns 0 rows (e.g., `embed_category` setting absent, blank, or not matching any category name), `[...] [0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migrated embeddable hosts are inserted raw via SQL, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization that strips http(s):// prefixes and paths, causing previously allowed hosts to fail matching and get Discourse::InvalidAccess on /embed/comments

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration copies SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts lines directly into the embeddable_hosts table via raw SQL: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. This bypasses the EmbeddableHost model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. After the change, allow-list checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` which parses the request URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If migrated rows contain values like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (explicitly shown as valid prior inputs in updated specs), they will not equal `discourse.org` / `example.com`, so previously-allowed hosts can start failing `host_allowed?` and trigger `Discourse::InvalidAccess` in EmbedController#ensure_embeddable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration permanently DELETEs the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings with no rollback path, causing unrecoverable data loss if any INSERT fails midway or rollback is needed

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses a `change` method but performs irreversible `execute` operations, including `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`. There is no `down` method to restore those site settings, so a rollback (or needing the old settings back after migrating) has no path to recover the deleted values. The part about “INSERT fails midway” is less accurate because migrations are typically run in a transaction (so partial changes would roll back), but the lack of a rollback path for the deleted settings is verifiably present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator file contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains only the EmbeddableHost fabricator while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the Category fabricators, misleading future contributors editing the wrong file

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` being replaced with a single `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition, while a new file `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:category)` plus related category variants (`:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). This is a clear swap/misnaming of fabricator file contents compared to their filenames and is verifiable directly in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embedding_controller.rb update action renders a serialization of the never-mutated @embedding, silently discarding all submitted changes from the PUT while responding 200 with success JSON

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddingController#update`, the code indeed just re-renders the current `@embedding` OpenStruct without applying any params. However, in this diff `@embedding` only contains `id` and `embeddable_hosts`, and host CRUD is implemented via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (create/update/destroy). The Ember template for embedding has no “save” button and the controller’s `saveChanges()` sends `update({})` (empty payload). So there are no actual submitted changes that would be expected to be persisted through `/customize/embedding` in the code shown; the finding claims a discard of changes that aren’t part of this implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update and destroy fetch EmbeddableHost by id with no nil check, causing NoMethodError and HTTP 500 instead of a 404 or validation error for stale or fabricated ids
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue points out that update and destroy retrieve EmbeddableHost by id without checking for nil, leading to NoMethodError/500 when the record doesn’t exist—same underlying problem described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic.rb expandable_first_post? dropped the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard, changing semantics so deleting all embeddable hosts no longer disables truncation for existing embedded topics

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Topic#expandable_first_post? from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. Since the `embeddable_hosts` site setting is removed and hosts are now stored in the EmbeddableHost table (and can be deleted), this condition no longer becomes false when there are zero allowed hosts. Therefore, if all EmbeddableHost records are deleted but a topic still has a TopicEmbed (`has_topic_embed?` true) and `embed_truncate` is enabled, `expandable_first_post?` will still return true, whereas previously it would have returned false when `embeddable_hosts` was blank. This is a real, verifiable semantic change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL string interpolation of unvalidated site setting values into raw INSERT in migration, allowing SQL injection or migration crash on single quotes

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration reads the existing `site_settings` value for `embeddable_hosts`, splits it into `h`, and then builds raw SQL with direct string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. If any `h` contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters), the migration can fail (syntax error) and, in principle, allows SQL injection during migration execution. There is no escaping/quoting via the DB connection (e.g., `quote`) or parameterization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unguarded nil on user-supplied params[:id] lookup in update and destroy actions of EmbeddableHostsController, causing unhandled 500 errors for stale or invalid ids

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy, the code fetches `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls methods on it (`save_host(host)` which does `host.host = ...`, and `host.destroy`). If the id is stale/invalid, `first` returns nil, leading to `NoMethodError` and an unhandled 500 response. There is no guard or 404 handling in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The entire spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController is only an ancestry assertion (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController), verifying none of the new behavior: the blank-category_id fallback to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id, the render_json_error path for invalid hosts, destroy of a nonexistent id (which would 500 on nil), or the serialization shape

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` contains only one example: `expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`. It does not exercise any of the newly added controller actions (`create`, `update`, `destroy`) or the key logic in `save_host` (e.g., `category_id` blank fallback to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, error handling via `render_json_error`, response/serialization shape). This is directly verifiable from the spec file contents shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update contains no persistence logic at all — it just re-renders the serialized @embedding — while the frontend saveChanges action calls update({}) expecting to save; no test issues a PUT and checks that anything changes, so the save embedding feature is a no-op that the passing suite gives false confidence about

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController` builds `@embedding` as an `OpenStruct` in `fetch_embedding` and both `show` and `update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` without reading any params or persisting anything. On the client, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which will issue a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` (routes + `admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6`). That PUT cannot change any state because the controller `update` action does no work besides re-rendering. Also, the added specs for `Admin::EmbeddingController` do not exercise PUT/update behavior or assert any change, so the suite would pass even though the update endpoint is a no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test in topic_spec.rb now verifies a branch that no longer exists after removal of the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard from Topic#expandable_first_post?; it passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false, and the new semantic (topic with has_topic_embed? and embed_truncate true is expandable even with zero hosts configured) has no coverage

The 'raises an error with a missing host' test in embed_controller_spec.rb is stale: it claims to cover host-config denial but passes only because no referer is stubbed, so the referer check fires instead; the new empty-hosts behavior (no rows in embeddable_hosts) is never directly asserted

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` no longer checks for a “no hosts configured” condition; it only raises unless `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`. In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the test still named "raises an error with a missing host" no longer sets any host configuration (the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil` line was removed) and also does not stub a referer. With no referer, `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(nil)` returns false (URI parsing fails and returns nil), so the request is rejected due to the referer check, not due to an empty `embeddable_hosts` table. Therefore the test is effectively stale/misleading and does not directly assert the behavior when there are zero `EmbeddableHost` rows but a valid referer is present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new plural _ids hydration branch in store.js.es6 is only tested on the happy path where all ids exist in the side-loaded payload; there is no test for an id absent from the root payload, where _lookupSubType returns null and the hydrated array silently contains null entries while the original _ids key is unconditionally deleted, crashing consumers like {{#each fruit.colors}} with unrecoverable data

The 'find embedded' test in store-test.js.es6 claims to load fruit 2 (banana, color_ids: [3]) but the pretender handler ignores the request id and always returns fruits[0] (apple, color_ids: [1,2]), so the assertions verify apple's data; the test passes only by mock accident and cannot catch hydration bugs specific to single-element color_ids arrays

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding refers to a specific test file (`store-test.js.es6`) and a Pretender handler behavior (ignoring request id and always returning `fruits[0]`). None of that code appears anywhere in the provided diff. The diff changes `discourse/models/store.js.es6` hydration logic and adds embedding-related UI/controllers/models, but it does not include or modify the referenced test or any Pretender mock setup for "fruits". Therefore the finding is not verifiable from this diff and does not identify a real problem introduced/shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The topic_embed.rb change replacing SiteSetting.embed_category with eh.try(:category_id) has only one spec assertion covering the matching-host case; no test exercises the branch where the imported URL's host is not registered (record_for_host returns nil), causing the topic to be created uncategorized instead of in the previously configured embed_category

adjudication.rationale: While it’s true the updated TopicEmbed.import now sets `category: eh.try(:category_id)` and the added spec only asserts the registered-host case, the claimed regression (“unregistered host now creates uncategorized instead of prior SiteSetting.embed_category”) isn’t a verifiable problem in this diff. The diff removes the `embed_category` setting entirely (`site_settings.yml` and `server.en.yml`, plus migration deletes it), so there is no longer a “previously configured embed_category” to fall back to. Additionally, unregistered hosts are now blocked earlier: both `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` were changed to require `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, so the branch where `record_for_host` returns nil/false should not be reachable in normal operation. The finding is therefore mainly about missing test coverage/speculation, not a concrete defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when the 'embed_category' setting row doesn't exist in site_settings or its value doesn't match a category name, because execute(...)[0] is nil on the default configuration

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does:

```rb
category_id = execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
```

If the query returns zero rows (e.g., there is no `site_settings` row named `embed_category`, or its `value` doesn’t match any `categories.name`), then `execute(...)[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError` before the later fallback `if category_id == 0` can run. This is a concrete crash scenario introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'uncategorized_category_id' fallback queries site_settings for a value that is a computed Ruby method on SiteSetting, not a database row, so the fallback path also crashes with NoMethodError

adjudication.rationale: The migration’s fallback does `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i`, which queries the `site_settings` DB table directly. The proposed finding claims `uncategorized_category_id` exists only as a computed Ruby method on `SiteSetting` and therefore there would be no DB row, causing a `NoMethodError`. Nothing in the diff supports that: the codebase already uses `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` elsewhere, and the migration is not calling that method at all. While the SQL could error if the row were missing (nil `[0]`), that’s an environment/data assumption not verifiable from this diff and not specifically tied to “computed Ruby method”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The migration irreversibly DELETEs the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site_settings rows inside def change with no down method, backup, or restore path, permanently losing configuration on rollback

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration is defined with `def change` and performs `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. That destructive SQL has no corresponding reverse operation (no `down` method, no re-insert/restore logic). On rollback, Rails cannot automatically restore deleted rows, so the previous configuration would be permanently lost (and the migration is effectively irreversible).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migrated host values are inserted verbatim without normalizing schemes/paths, so hosts stored as 'http://discourse.org' never match the new EmbeddableHost.record_for_host query comparing against uri.host, silently breaking previously-allowed embeds

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, existing SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts values are copied into embeddable_hosts via raw SQL: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. This bypasses EmbeddableHost’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. After the change, embedding checks use `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` which calls `record_for_host` and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If the migrated DB value is `http://discourse.org` (or includes a path), it will not equal `discourse.org`, so previously-allowed hosts can stop matching post-migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host values are interpolated into raw SQL INSERT statements without quoting or parameterization, allowing syntax errors or SQL injection from single quotes/backslashes in stored values
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue flag the same underlying security problem: raw SQL is constructed via string interpolation of host values (e.g., '#{h}') without parameter binding/proper quoting, which can lead to SQL injection (and related syntax issues).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The deploy removes the settings from site_settings.yml and deletes SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? in the same step as the data migration, so old application servers during a rolling restart raise undefined-method/missing-setting errors with no expand/contract transitional phase
